description:
Job Title: Data Architect ETL & Data Warehousing (BFSI Focus)
Location: Chennai
Employment Type: Permanent
Experience: 10–15 years
The Data Architect will lead the design, modernization, and optimization of enterprise data
ecosystems, focusing on ETL, data warehousing, and cloud data solutions. BFSI experience is highly preferred due to domain-specific requirements involving regulatory reporting, customer data, risk systems, and core banking data flows.
This role requires more than just following instructions we need someone who proactively identifies issues, understands the "why" behind the request, and takes ownership of designing and implementing solutions. Flexibility beyond assigned roles is key in our culture.
Key Responsibilities:
Work closely with business units and product teams to elicit and structure often-implicit data requirements and convert them into business relevant information.
Design enterprise-scale data architecture across ingestion, ETL/ELT, warehousing, and analytics layers.
Build data models (conceptual, logical, physical) tailored to BFSI domains such as deposits, lending, payments, KYC, AML, credit risk, regulatory reporting, and treasury.
Architect ETL/ELT pipelines using Databrics, Azure.
Design and optimize data warehouse and data mart solutions (Kimball/Inmon/Data Vault).
Implement cloud-native data solutions on Azure with focus on security,
compliance, and performance.
Ensure adherence to BFSI regulatory standards (RBI, Basel, IFRS, GDPR Any of these).
Collaborate with business, risk, compliance, and IT teams to translate BFSI data needs into scalable architecture.
Define and enforce standards for data governance, lineage, metadata, and data quality.
Conduct impact analysis and stakeholder communication when new data sources or structural changes are introduced to the system.
Required Skills & Experience:
10–15 years in data architecture, engineering, and warehousing.
Strong experience in BFSI data platforms—core banking, risk systems, AML/KYC platforms, data lakes for regulatory needs.
Expertise in ETL tools: ETL, data engineering, data warehousing, governance, and cloud transformation, Databricks, Data analytics and Azure data pipeline
Hands-on experience with Databrics, Bigdata or Oracle.
Strong SQL, data modeling, and distributed data processing. – Any database will work –
PL SQL is preferred
Experience with cloud data services and big data tools like Spark or Databricks.
Professional Skills:
Strong analytical mindset with excellent problem-solving and critical-thinking abilities.
Excellent communication and storytelling skills to convey complex analyses to non-technical stakeholders.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver under tight timelines.
Proactive, innovative, and collaborative attitude with a passion for continuous learning.
Experience working with BFSI compliance, governance, and risk management teams.
Good to have:
Experience working with non-technical stakeholders.
Experience working in or with Japanese-oriented companies or clients.
Databricks certification or equivalent cloud platform credentials (e.g., AWS/Azure/ GCP).
Education:
Bachelor’s or Master’s in Computer Science, Information Systems, or related fields.
Cloud or data architecture certifications preferred.

title: Data Architect
description:
Data Architect Healthcare Workflows (Psych Bonus)
Own canonical JSONs, provenance fields, deltas/patches, and taxonomies across our clinical workflows. Your work ensures data consistency, traceability, and reliability , enabling safer and more effective patient care. Familiarity with the clinical mental health domain is a bonus, augmented by collaboration with domain experts like Ravi.
Values Vibe (Who You Are)
We want a meticulous, thoughtful data architect who thrives on structure, clarity, and safety . You care about data quality and consistency, and you communicate clearly with engineers, product managers, and clinicians. You enjoy designing robust data models that empower teams to ship reliable features while maintaining clinical accuracy.
A Day in Flow (The Feel, Not a Script)
Morning: review delta/patch operations, check schema validation reports, and ensure provenance fields are correct.
During sprints: define canonical patient JSONs, versioning semantics, and mapping rules across modules.
Afternoon: collaborate on safety flags, ungroundedness checks, and billing-related data clarity; update documentation and data dictionaries. Quiet impact, zero drama.
What You ll Own
Canonical JSONs Data Models: Design and maintain canonical patient JSONs and provenance fields for assessments and workflows.
Deltas, Patches Versioning: Define delta/patch semantics, versioning, and mapping across modules to ensure data consistency.
Safety Compliance Collaboration: Work with engineers and clinicians on safety/ungroundedness flags and billing clarity.
Documentation Knowledge Sharing: Maintain clear documentation, schemas, and taxonomies to support engineering and clinical teams.
Domain Expertise Augmentation: Integrate clinical mental health specifics with guidance from subject matter experts.
Authority (Ramped on Purpose)
You ll own the data architecture standards for clinical workflows from day one. Scope ramps as you deliver: enforce JSON schema best practices, maintain provenance, ensure safe versioning, and escalate inconsistencies or potential data risks early with full team support.
Schedule (India)
Works daytime hours with 4-8 hours of overlap to US Pacific (e.g., 11:00am-7:00pm CT / 9:00am-5:00pm PT), with flexibility for cross-functional sessions with engineers and clinical experts.
What Success Looks Like
Canonical JSONs are consistent, validated, and integrated across all workflows.
Delta/patch versioning is robust, traceable, and reliable.
Safety and ungroundedness flags are effective and actionable.
Billing and clinical data mapping are clear and maintainable.
Teams rely on your data architecture for correctness, safety, and efficiency.
What You ve Done
4+ years in data modeling , JSON schema design, and event sourcing/versioning.
Strong experience in defining canonical data structures, provenance models, and deltas/patches.
Familiarity with healthcare data is a plus; mental health domain experience is highly valued.
Excellent communication and collaboration across technical and clinical teams.
Preferred: experience designing data taxonomies, clinical data pipelines, or event-driven architectures.
Benefits
Remote-first across India
Equipment stipend
Local holidays (India)
Learning budget for data modeling, healthcare workflows, and clinical data best practices
Job Type: Full-time Remote
